clue.text: Girl without one Parisian black gown

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name goes around the figure for one

parts.note: Peg is a short form of the girl's name Margaret
the Roman numeral I stands for one
noir is the French word for black, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A girl without a single French black dress to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the girl goes around the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a woman's light loose dressing gown or negligee.

clue.text: Look into horse's food

indicators.note: into tells us the word for look goes inside the horse word

parts.note: a pony is a small horse
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Inspect a horse's feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Polony is a type of seasoned pork sausage, a dish to eat.

clue.text: Elected officer, as a rule

parts.note: a winning candidate is in, voted into office
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: An officer is elected as normal practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean usually, on the whole.

clue.text: Ruffles not entirely superfluous.

indicators.note: not entirely means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: needless means unnecessary, superfluous

explanation.surface: Frills on a garment are not wholly unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruffles' is a verb, as in ruffling someone's feathers; drop the last S of NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or provoke them.

clue.text: Used once in stir, on some

definitions.text: Used once in stir, on some

indicators.note: in shows the answer is lodged within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something formerly used in prison, on some inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for prison; the answer lies inside 'stir, on some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are fetters or shackles, formerly put on some prisoners in jail.

clue.text: Person controlling the pack has an ace

definitions.meaning: a ... of hounds is in charge of a pack of foxhounds
an ace is an expert, someone with complete command of a skill

explanation.surface: The leader of the group holds the ace in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pack' suggests a pack of cards beside 'ace', but it is a pack of hounds; in British foxhunting the Master of Foxhounds runs the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunt's master directs the hounds, and a master of a craft is a virtuoso or expert.

clue.text: A lot of trouble for Lady Masham

parts.note: big money is a lot of money
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: An aristocratic lady faces a great deal of difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Abigail Masham, Lady Masham, was Queen Anne's favourite at court.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Masham's first name was Abigail; she was a lady-in-waiting and royal confidante.

clue.text: In which a toast could be: drunk to King Arthur's foster brother

definitions.text: In which a toast could be: drunk

parts.note: taken as written
Sir Kay was raised with Arthur in the legends

explanation.surface: A toast raised to Sir Kay of Arthurian legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk to' reads as raising a toast to someone; 'to' is actually part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine, something one raises a glass of.

clue.text: Turning up to put sailor outside

indicators.note: outside means the sailor word encloses the other piece

parts.note: a rating is a non-commissioned sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word to is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Changing course to put a seaman out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' turns 'to' backwards, and 'outside' wraps the sailor around the result; 'put' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating means spinning round on an axis.

clue.text: After a considerable time, books become self-indulgent

indicators.note: after places the books abbreviation following the time period

parts.note: a decade is ten years, a considerable time
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: After many years, reading turns hedonistic.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is a common crossword abbreviation for books; 'become' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes someone given to luxury and moral decline.

clue.text: Member already at gate by which one can get out

definitions.text: by which one can get out

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
before means previously, already at an earlier time
a wicket is a small gate, often set in a larger one

explanation.surface: A limb already at the gate of an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is out leg before wicket (LBW) when the ball hits his leg where it would otherwise have struck the stumps. 'get out' sounds like escape, but it is a cricket dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is one of the standard ways a batsman can be dismissed by the umpire.

clue.text: Puzzle not involving addition

parts.note: non is a prefix meaning not
plus is the sign and word used for addition in arithmetic

explanation.surface: A sum that doesn't require any adding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' is a verb here: to baffle someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to bewilder or perplex them so they cannot respond.

clue.text: One who breaks down a recorder, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a recorder is heard spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: an annalist is a chronicler who records events year by year

explanation.surface: Someone who dismantles a recorder, the woodwind instrument, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' looks like the musical instrument or a tape machine; it is a keeper of annals. 'One who breaks down' means someone who examines things in parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst examines something by separating it into its constituent parts.

clue.text: Uncorrupted element in, force

indicators.note: in tells us the element's symbol word sits inside the word for force

parts.note: to prise is to force open with leverage
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A pure chemical element in effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine means in its original, unspoilt condition, untouched by decay.

clue.text: Ultimately mean middleman

indicators.note: middle tells us the male pronoun sits in the centre of the word for mean

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: In the final reckoning, a stingy go-between.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'middle man' as two words. The surface reads as a stingy go-between, but 'mean' is a verb and 'middle' puts the man in its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean eventually, after everything has happened.

clue.text: The answer often is returned, "No, Honey"

definitions.text: The answer often is returned, "No, Honey"

indicators.note: returned means the words for no and honey are read back to front together

parts.note: mel is the Latin word for honey, familiar from pharmacy

explanation.surface: A suitor's proposal is often met with a gentle refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: NO followed by MEL, reversed together by 'returned', gives the answer. The whole clue also hints at an unappealing person, a dud, who is often turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a dud or a dull, unattractive person, the kind who hears refusals.

clue.text: Holy, by the sound of it not a theme to be, misinterpreted

definitions.text: Holy, by the sound of it
definitions.note: holy said aloud is holey, full of holes

indicators.note: misinterpreted means read wrongly, so the words' letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something sacred, it seems, is no subject for misreading.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the spoken sense: 'Holy' sounds like holey. 'to be' links to the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten cloth is riddled with holes made by moth larvae.

clue.text: Babies are' often revolting

definitions.meaning: babies are often carried in someone's embrace

explanation.surface: Infants are frequently disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgusting but means rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants are held in the embrace, and protesters in rebellion are indignant.

clue.text: Plant troops within hearing

indicators.note: within hearing signals the word for troops is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to troop is to flock, move together in a crowd

explanation.surface: Soldiers stationed close enough to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troops' looks like a noun for soldiers but is a verb: flocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a flowering garden plant with clusters of bright blooms.

clue.text: Making picture unsuitable for kids, with man wearing gorilla's. head

parts.note: X was the British film certificate for adults only
Ray is a man's name
in can mean wearing, as in dressed in a suit

indicators.note: the head of gorilla is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shooting an adult film with an actor in a gorilla mask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making picture' suggests a film shoot, but it is a radiograph; X was the old British adults-only film rating.
explanation.definitionFit: X-raying produces a radiograph, an image of the body's inside.

clue.text: Bird that's circling vessel seen to preen

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: circling shows the abbreviation for that is goes round the container word

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a vat is a large vessel for liquids

explanation.surface: A bird circling a ship is seen grooming its feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for i.e. ('that is'), which 'circling' puts around the vessel; 'seen to' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To titivate is to smarten oneself up, fuss over one's appearance.

clue.text: Tasteful extract from worn-out bible read the wrong way

indicators.note: read the wrong way means the words for worn-out and bible run backwards together

parts.note: all in means exhausted, worn out
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A tasteful passage from a tattered Bible read backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL IN then AV, reversed together by 'read the wrong way', gives the answer; 'from' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla extract is a flavouring essence drawn from the vanilla pod.

clue.text: 5 changes in course

indicators.note: changes signals the letters of the referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: refers to the answer at 5 across

explanation.surface: A captain's switches as he steers the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a watercourse, a small river.

clue.text: Cook can't use one that's touched

indicators.note: to cook is to fiddle or doctor, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef unable to use something that's been handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a chef but is the anagram signal; 'touched' means slightly mad, not handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Touched is slang for crazy, and a nutcase is a crazy person.

clue.text: Bent, in a sense

definitions.meaning: one of the five senses, perceiving flavour

explanation.definitionFit: Taste means a liking or inclination, and also the sense of flavour.

clue.text: The capacity to please

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to satisfy someone

explanation.definitionFit: Content is the amount contained (volume), and to content someone is to satisfy them.

clue.text: Monster standing on his head, riding horseback

indicators.note: in a down clue standing on his head means the monster word is turned upside down

parts.note: an orc is a goblin-like monster
up means on horseback, riding

explanation.surface: A monster doing a headstand while riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseback' here means the back of a horse: its rump.
explanation.definitionFit: The croup is the rump or hindquarters of a horse, behind the saddle.

clue.text: Game results are out, in chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The scores come out amid confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in chaos' looks like one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a deadly game of chance with a revolver containing one bullet.

clue.text: Apprentice rushes around to find tool

indicators.note: around shows the plant word is wrapped round the learner's letter

parts.note: sedge is a grass-like marsh plant, like rushes
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee hurries about looking for an implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rushes' looks like a verb for hurrying, but it is the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is a sledgehammer, a heavy long-handled hammer.

clue.text: Hangs up variegated geranium, the end in moss

indicators.note: variegated means of mixed colours, signalling a jumbled order of letters
the end of geranium is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gardener hangs up a multicoloured geranium in a moss-lined basket.
explanation.walkthrough: HANGSUP rearranged gives SPHAGNU, then the final M of geranium; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sphagnum is bog moss, used by gardeners to line hanging baskets.
